question: Should OpenClaw core grow a per-agent backup/restore/clone CLI surface, and what credential/session portability policy should it use?
rationale: The implementation would add new CLI flags and restore behavior that rewrites sensitive per-agent config, credentials, SQLite state, workspaces, and sessions, so automation cannot choose the product and security contract safely.

options.title: Sponsor a core design
options.body: Define a first-party per-agent archive/restore contract, including explicit rules for auth profiles, transcripts, path rewrites, rollback, and clone ids.

options.title: Fold into broader backup work
options.body: Keep this issue open but require the broader backup/restore effort to explicitly cover per-agent `--agent` and `--as` semantics before it lands.

options.title: Decline core clone
options.body: Document manual or external tooling as the supported path and close only after maintainers decide core should not own per-agent clone/restore.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core design
recommendation.body: Define a first-party per-agent archive/restore contract, including explicit rules for auth profiles, transcripts, path rewrites, rollback, and clone ids.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent backup SQLite snapshot and release-surface work makes Vincent the strongest available routing candidate for the backup restore safety decision.
